data.name: Edyth
data.gender_notes: Edyth is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek word 'edýomai', meaning 'to yield or produce', or 'edytho', meaning 'wealth' or 'prosperity'. The name Edyth was popular among early Christians due to its association with abundance and prosperity. The name Edyth carries the meaning “Wealth, prosperity” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Edyth usually hope their child will grow to embody wealth, prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of abundance and prosperity in life
data.etymology: Edyth belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wealth, prosperity.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Edyth total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Edyth was popular among early Christians in the medieval period, particularly those who valued the idea of productivity and prosperity. It may have been given to children in the hope that they would grow up to be successful, hardworking members of their communities.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Edyth holds a deeper spiritual significance beyond just prosperity and productivity. It is seen as a reminder of God's abundance and provision in our lives. Edyth may also symbolize the idea of spiritual wealth, which cannot be measured in earthly terms but is rather a richness of the soul. Ultimately, the name Edyth invites us to reflect on the biblical promise that "God will supply all our needs according to his glorious riches in Christ Jesus" (Philippians 4:19).
